method: Flesch-Kincaid grade with a transparent vowel-group syllable heuristic; estimated age = grade + 5, floored at zero. Count sentences using terminal punctuation. Exact measured corpora included. This is a rough editorial screen, not a learner assessment. Teacher-only text excluded.

corpora.text: I can use still poses to tell a short story. I can show first, next and last. I can choose a pose or direct one. I can keep one real choice in my arts log. Choose act, direct or watch first. Point, speak, sign or pass. Use made-up roles today. Watch a still pose: look at an empty shelf. What might be lost? Watch a smile and a point. What may come next? Watch first, next and last. First: the prop is lost. Next: the helper looks in a box. Last: the prop is found. Choose a helper and a friend. Pick first, next and last. Try three still poses with space. Which pose helps us see the end? In your book, mark first, next and last. Use our story or make a safe new one. Try three poses. Keep space. Change one pose to help the viewer. Tell an adult what you chose. Choose one pose to show. You may show just the adult. Say: I notice ___. Relax and clear your space. Arts log: I showed ___. I chose ___ because ___. Next time I will ___. A still pose that shows one part of a story. A made-up person in a story. A sign to start or stop. Things that happen in an order.

Pick lost prop or folded sheet. Choose first, next and last with an adult. Make a seated pose or direct the adult. Point to one pose to keep in your log. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Plan first, next and last in your book. Rehearse three poses with a partner. Ask what the viewer can see. Change one pose and log your reason. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Use the same three-part task. Try two ways to show the ending. Choose the clearer one. Say why. Give your partner a calm start cue. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

A helper looks at an empty shelf. The helper pauses with open hands. A friend points to a box. They both look in the box. They smile when the prop is found. What shows the problem? How does a still pose help us follow the story? Two makers hold an imaginary large sheet. They stop when it will not fit. One points to a fold. They fold the sheet in mime, then carry it together with space between them. What changes after the pause? How does the second action show a new plan? I notice ___. I could use ___ in my own scene because ___. These are invented class models. They are not pupil work.

Look at an empty shelf with empty hands. Say: First, the prop is lost. Point into an imaginary box. Say: Next, I search. Hold an imaginary prop. Say: Last, I find it. Turn the last pose towards the viewer. Say: I changed this so you can see the end. Choose your role. Try a short scene. Change one thing. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

Use freeze-frame/role-play to tell a story. I can show first, next and last. I can choose a pose or direct one. I can keep one real choice in my arts log. freeze-frame: A still pose that shows one part of a story. role: A made-up person in a story. cue: A sign to start or stop. story: Things that happen in an order. Use a made-up story. Keep your own space. Stop on the open hand. You can sit, stay silent or direct. You may share with just the adult.

I can add a short action or line to our story. I can keep first, next and last clear. I can add one action or short line. I can share and log a real choice. Choose act, direct or sit. Find your story plan if it is here. A fresh plan is fine. Show or direct one still pose. Is it first, next or last? What could the role say? Watch a pose, a line and a move. I say: Where is the prop? I look in the box. I say: Here it is! Then I freeze. Pick one line or silent action. Try it between two poses. Give a calm cue. Ask: Could you follow the story? Use your plan or make a fresh one. Add one move or short line. Keep voices calm and leave space. Try it, ask for one note, then try again. Log what you chose. Share a small part or the whole story. Choose your audience. Say: I saw ___ in your story. Put plans away with care. Arts log: I added ___. Our viewer noticed ___. Next time I will ___. Act as a made-up person in a story. Words a role says. Show an action without a real object. A short stop.

Use the lost prop plan. Choose one short line or a silent move. Act seated or direct an adult. Keep one choice in your arts log. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Use or make a three-part plan. Add a line, mime or pause. Rehearse and ask for one clear note. Try a change and log what helped. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Keep the same core story task. Try a silent version and a spoken one. Choose which tells the story best. Explain the effect of your pause or cue. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Show empty hands. Say: Where is the prop? Mime looking in a box. Keep the body in personal space. Pause, show an imaginary prop and say: Here it is! Repeat the last part facing the viewer. Say: I chose a pause so the end was clear. Choose your role. Try a short scene. Change one thing. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

Use freeze-frame/role-play to tell a story. I can keep first, next and last clear. I can add one action or short line. I can share and log a real choice. role-play: Act as a made-up person in a story. line: Words a role says. mime: Show an action without a real object. pause: A short stop. Use a made-up story. Keep your own space. Stop on the open hand. You can sit, stay silent or direct. You may share with just the adult.

I can select real arts evidence and explain one choice. I can find or make a genuine dated entry. I can explain what I did and the help I used. I can choose evidence and a safe audience to share it. Choose a private or small audience. Gather the arts logs that are here. If yours is missing, use today's fresh task. Compare: a blank log and a real dated entry. Which shows what happened? What extra detail would help? Watch an adult sort model evidence. Find: what, when, my part, my choice. Mark clear, needs a note or missing. Keep model evidence separate from your own. Try one record together with permission. Ask: What did the maker do? Ask: What choice is shown? Choose one clear item or one honest gap. In your arts log, select up to three real items. For each, find a date and your part. Choose one item you could explain. If no work is here, make a tiny drama now. Plan one real gap to fill later. Explain one selected item to your chosen viewer. Say: My part was ___. Viewer asks: What helped your idea? Store the work for Wednesday. I selected or made ___. This shows I ___. My next step before sharing is ___. Real work or a record of what you actually did. A collection of your arts work and records. The part you chose or did. Something that still needs a real record.

Review one real item with an adult. Point to your part or explain it aloud. If no item is here, direct a two-pose drama. Keep a dated note and choose a viewer. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Audit up to three available items. Record each date, your part and one choice. Select an item and one honest gap. Plan a short share with an agreed audience. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Complete the same real-evidence audit. Compare two items for what they show. Explain which best shows a choice and why. Set one precise evidence or skill goal. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Compare two real items. Explain which gives clearer evidence of your choice and why. Identify one skill goal and plan how you will check it. Keep item references, your own comparison, the reason and a specific future check. Date new notes today.

I can share genuine arts evidence and use one useful response. I can explain my contribution and a choice. I can share with an agreed audience. I can record a response and a real next step. Choose your audience again. Find Monday's selected item. If it is missing, use today's fresh task. Listen to two viewer responses. Which helps the maker? You are good, or Your pause showed the change. Watch a short evidence share. This is the item. My part was ___. I chose ___ because ___. Ask one viewer question. Rehearse your share with a partner or adult. Name the item, your part and a choice. Viewer says: I notice ___. Maker confirms or explains. Prepare a short share with your chosen viewer. Use a real item, or make a fresh tiny drama. Explain one choice and its reason. Listen to one response. Log what you will keep or change. Name a choice you want to keep. Name a small change, if one would help. Check your viewer note is true. Put the item back in your log. I shared ___ with ___. They noticed ___. I will ___ because ___. The person or people you choose to share with. A specific response that can help your next choice. The actual item or record you are explaining. Your thoughts about what you did and what comes next.

Choose one real item or a fresh two-pose task. Use the frame My part was ___. Share with one agreed viewer. Confirm one note and a next step. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.
